rules.title: An object shape declared outside the domain model
rules.fix: Declare the entity, value object or view in src/domain (or derive it there from the schema with drizzle-zod) and import it. A screen-only shape belongs in src/domain/views.

rules.title: any, as unknown as, or a suppressed type error
rules.fix: Give the value its domain type. If it comes from outside (a request, a JSON column, an API), parse it with the domain's zod schema instead of asserting.

rules.title: A type assertion to a named type (trusting a shape instead of parsing it)
rules.fix: Parse at the boundary with the domain schema (Schema.parse(x)) so a wrong shape fails loudly where it enters, not three layers later.

rules.title: A json/jsonb column with no declared shape
rules.fix: Give the column .$type<DomainShape>() and a matching zod schema in src/domain, or make the shape its own table if anything filters, joins or sums on it.

rules.title: A nullable column whose null has no written meaning
rules.fix: Either add .notNull(), or write what null means in a comment just above the column, e.g. /** null means: not answered yet */. One meaning, decided once, so no screen can pick its own.

rules.title: Schema changed from application code instead of a migration
rules.fix: Change src/db/schema.ts, run npm run db:generate, and commit the migration with a decision record (docs/decisions).

rules.title: Optional chaining or ?? in a screen or component
rules.fix: A screen receives a parsed domain view whose fields are present or explicitly optional. If a field can be missing, make that a state in the view type (e.g. status: 'unanswered'), not a silent fallback.

rules.title: A screen or the domain imports the database
rules.fix: Screens get data from src/server (the one read path); the domain receives plain values. src/domain may import src/db/schema (declarations only, to derive its zod shapes), never the client or queries.

rules.title: I/O, time or randomness inside the pure domain
rules.fix: Pass today, ids and fetched data in as parameters. The domain is pure so every rule has exactly one testable definition.
